metadata.title: Claude, Matter Update.
metadata.subtitle: One Skill, Read Fresh Every Time
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Teardown register: when Claude logs an update on a legal matter the same way every time, is that memory of your firm's habits, or something else? Lands the carry-out that a Claude skill is a file it reads fresh, every time — not a memory of your workflow.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B09 (Case 4471: an offer planted, then logged)
metadata.one_flag: N/A - facts locked from source narration, no inference introduced (see SCRIPT.md One-flag audit)

beats.narration_text: The obvious guess: Claude remembers how your firm logs a matter update — same shape, run enough times. Wrong branch. Nothing carries over between conversations. So where do the steps actually come from?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'How does Claude remember how our firm logs a case update?', hesitates on 'remember', corrects to 'know', lands the real question

props.text:

remember how our
firm logs a case

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('remember' -> 'know') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Here's what's actually happening on a legal team. Every open matter keeps moving — a filing lands, an offer comes in, a deadline shifts — and every change has to get logged the same way, every time, across every case. Uniform records is the constraint. That's the job.

shot.new_visual_element: Five kinds of change, one matter

production_viz.label: Five kinds of change, one matter
production_viz.mechanic: A row of five plain chips naming the kinds of change a matter goes through, fading in left to right on cream.

beats.narration_text: Pin one case: Case forty-four seventy-one. A settlement offer just landed. It needs to hit the record — same fields, same shape as every other case. Hold onto it; we'll come back to see exactly what happens.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — Case 4471, an offer arrives

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — Case 4471, an offer arrives
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Two chips: 'CASE 4471' and 'SETTLEMENT OFFER', connected by an arrow. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS AT B09.

beats.narration_text: The easy reading is that Claude picks up habits the way a new paralegal does — do it enough, it just learns how you work here. Familiar model of learning: use, remember, repeat. That's the intuition. It's also wrong, and the test is one line long.

production_viz.label: The fixed-memory reading
production_viz.mechanic: Three chips in sequence — USE IT ONCE, USE IT AGAIN, IT REMEMBERS US — with the last one accented, selling the reading as reasonable.

beats.narration_text: Open a fresh conversation — new session, a matter Claude has never seen — and ask for the same kind of update. The exact same steps run, immediately. Nothing crossed over. Whatever's driving the behavior wasn't stored in the last chat; it wasn't stored anywhere between them.

production_viz.label: A fresh conversation breaks it
production_viz.mechanic: 'IT REMEMBERS US' struck through in muted tone; beside it 'SAME STEPS, INSTANTLY' accented — a brand-new, untouched matter runs identically.

beats.narration_text: Here's what's actually there: a Skill. A folder Claude reads before it does anything. This one's named matter-update. Not code, not a plugin — a directory with a text file in it.

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: Two chips — 'matter-update/' and 'SKILL.md' — connected by an arrow, the file accented as the thing Claude reads.

beats.narration_text: Inside is one instruction, in plain English: append a dated event to the matter's history file, then refresh the log row to match. Two moves, in that order. That's the whole recipe.

production_viz.label: The one instruction
production_viz.mechanic: Two chips — 'APPEND DATED EVENT' and 'REFRESH LOG ROW' — joined by an arrow, both plain, no accent (this is simply what the file says).

beats.narration_text: It fires for exactly five kinds of change: a new development, a status change, a risk re-assessment, a deadline shift, a change in settlement authority. Everything else, the skill doesn't touch. Scope is what the file says, no more.

production_viz.label: Five triggers
production_viz.mechanic: A row of five chips naming the exact triggers — development, status change, risk re-assessment, deadline shift, authority change.

beats.narration_text: The mechanic is boring on purpose. Claude reads the file first, every single run, then walks the steps top to bottom. Linear. No branching unless a step says otherwise. Same input, same list, same result — that's the whole point.

production_viz.label: Read, then act, in order
production_viz.mechanic: Four chips in a line — 'READ SKILL.md', 'STEP 1', 'STEP 2', 'STEP 3' — connected by arrows, straight through with no branch.

beats.narration_text: Back to Case forty-four seventy-one. The offer becomes a dated event in the history file. The log row updates to match. That's the recipe finishing — not a memory of this case, not a habit picked up from your firm. The file said do this; it did this.

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — Case 4471, logged
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical: 'CASE 4471' and 'SETTLEMENT OFFER', both now accented — done, per the file's recipe.

beats.narration_text: Ask for exactly what the file describes — a dated event, a refreshed row — and you get the same output every time, on any matter, from any conversation. That's the design win. Reliability is a consequence of narrowing the job to what's written.

production_viz.label: Exactly what's written, reliably
production_viz.mechanic: Two chips — 'EXACTLY WHAT'S WRITTEN' and 'SAME RESULT, EVERY TIME' — joined by an arrow, the second accented.

beats.narration_text: Ask for something the file never mentions — a strategy call, a new field, a judgment about whether the offer is any good — and there's nothing to run. It doesn't guess. That's the trade-off: the skill does only what's written. Judgment isn't in the file, so judgment isn't on the menu.

shot.new_visual_element: Not in the file, no guess

production_viz.label: Not in the file, no guess
production_viz.mechanic: Mirroring B10: three chips — 'STRATEGY CALL', 'NEW FIELD', 'NOT WRITTEN DOWN' — all muted, nothing accented (there is no guess to accent).

beats.narration_text: Claude's skill isn't a memory of your firm's habits — it's a file it reads fresh, every single time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. I want to understand how a Skill works in Claude — a folder with a plain-English file, SKILL.md, that Claude reads before acting, every single run. I have a repeated task I do at work: [describe it in one sentence]. Write me a SKILL.md for it. Include the triggers — the five or so situations that should set it off. The steps, in numbered order, plain English, no code. What not to touch. And what to hand back to me at the end. Then tell me what you left out, and why. Go deeper: ask the same model to run the SKILL.md it just wrote against three variants of the task — one clean, one edge case, one where the steps clearly don't cover the situation — and describe what the skill would do, and refuse to do, in each.

Include (1) the triggers — the five or so situations that should set it off, (2) the steps in numbered order, plain English, no code, (3) what NOT to touch, and (4) what to hand back to me at the end. Then tell me what you left out, and why.
